2_step2b.ATTRIBUTION_NOTE: A combined count that cannot be attributed is not a pass (addendum 12 item 5), so each mechanism is also run ALONE against rung 3. Read the three one-factor rows before the headline.

3_characteristic_decision._the_question: D230 (2): count guard activations attributable to the ALERT channel under the new thresholds and confirm non-zero. The as-built guard managed 16 across four seeds.
3_characteristic_decision.WHY_THE_ALERT_COUNT_IS_ZERO_AND_WHAT_THA: *** A DRY CELL CANNOT TEST THIS AND THE ZERO IS NOT A NEGATIVE. *** `coordinator._dry_service_s` returns `costs.episodic_cloud_latency_s('32BI', 1, 25)` for EVERY monitor request: a CONSTANT 0.394966 s with no queueing term. The dry alert EWMA therefore takes exactly TWO values in a whole cell (0.0 before the first completion and 0.394966 after it) and CANNOT reach 0.8 s in any period. Assistance is the same shape at a different number. This is CLAUDE.md Rule 2's `unexercised` and it is a property of the dry harness, not of the variant. An OBSERVED alert-channel count can only come from a cell with a real engine under queueing, i.e. the s4 GPU cell, and it is PRE-REGISTERED as a check on that cell.

POSITIVE_CONTROL_the_branch_is_reachable._what: The same arm and the same cell with ONLY the alert threshold moved to 0.3 s, BELOW the dry constant, through the PRODUCTION setter `arms_final_ladder._set_per_type_guard`. If the alert branch could not reach a decision at all this would also fire zero times and move zero decisions. IT IS A REACHABILITY CONTROL, NOT A RESULT, and 0.3 s is not a threshold anyone proposes.

comparison.label: ptg vs ptg with ALERT threshold at 0.3 s

CONSTRUCTED_EXPECTATION_for_the_s4_cell.register: CONSTRUCTED BOUND from a validated replay: D230's own positive control reproduced the committed `guard_by_lag` to within 0 to 3 epochs in 12,000 at every seed, and every fraction there is a LOWER bound (missing request.jsonl rows). NOT an observed count from any cell this build ran.
CONSTRUCTED_EXPECTATION_for_the_s4_cell.why_it_is_not_an_equality: 251 is neither a prediction nor a bar. The per-type guard also moves the RECALL bar from 2.0 to 2.4 s and adds the latch, both of which change which requests are warmed and therefore the EWMA trajectory itself. The replay is of the as-built arm's trace, so it says what the alert channel DID, not what it will do once the policy reacts differently.

4_negative_controls._what: The variant adds TWO mechanisms, so there are two controls and they are run separately. The machinery stays FULLY LIVE in both: switch on, strict reader passing, the per-type block executing, the log written.

control_A_thresholds_disabled._how: All three per-type thresholds set to the committed single 2.0 s bar AND the latch off. That is the only setting that can collapse to rung 3 exactly, because a control that left the latch on would fail for a reason other than the thing being controlled.
control_A_thresholds_disabled.RESIDUAL_RISK_STATED: The collapse is exact here and is NOT exact by construction. The committed test is `max(episodic, recall) >= 2.0`; the per-type test at 2.0/2.0/2.0 is `any(episodic, recall, ASSISTANCE >= 2.0)`, which also tests the THIRD channel. The two agree in this cell only because the dry assistance EWMA never reaches 2.0 s. On a cell where assistance lag exceeds 2.0 s the control would differ, and that difference would be the third channel doing its job, not a defect.

control_B_hysteresis_disabled._how: The same variant with the latch off, which is the -nohyst arm.

comparison.label: ptg-nohyst vs ptg (the LATCH on top)

control_B_hysteresis_disabled.VERDICT: THE LATCH CHANGES THE RESULT: 6145 positional differences, so the mechanism is driving something

control_A_MEASURED_AGREEMENT_not_argued._what: The residual risk states that control A collapses only because the dry assistance channel never reaches 2.0 s. That is an ARGUMENT. These are the numbers that make it an OBSERVATION. Added to THIS run's artefact from THIS run's own committed per-period guard logs (cells rung3_with_only_the_log and ctl20_neither); the proof script now emits the same block natively, so every future run carries it without back-filling.
control_A_MEASURED_AGREEMENT_not_argued.WHY_THE_COMMITTED_COUNT_IS_THE_RIGHT_COM: `rung3_with_only_the_log` runs the COMMITTED two-channel `max(episodic, recall) >= 2.0` test and logs it, so its activation count is the committed guard's own behaviour ON THIS CELL. Control A runs `any(episodic, assistance, recall >= 2.0)`. Equal counts (1,046 = 1,046) plus an assistance channel that peaks at 0.302256 s with 1.697744 s of headroom and NEVER crosses is the evidence that the third channel contributed nothing here, established independently of the byte-identical digest rather than inferred from it.
control_A_MEASURED_AGREEMENT_not_argued.register: OBSERVED, from this run's own per-period guard logs. Not a re-run and not a re-derivation.

The branch is REACHABLE (control: 11935 alert firings, 13946 decisions moved). The recall channel DID fire 681 times and the D166 (3) latch held the guard active in 1201 periods with no entry, so the variant's other characteristic decisions ARE non-zero. The alert count is PRE-REGISTERED as a check on the s4 GPU cell.
